## Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900

**My pick is the <Entity category="product" value="BLUETTI AC200L" disambig="2048Wh LiFePO4 portable power station"/>**, especially if you want to plug your RV directly into the power station.

  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product photo front three quarter view" aspectRatio="3:4" maxWidth="148px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <title size="lg">BLUETTI AC200L</title>
    <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums={true}>$854.05</title>

    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Reported in stock October 31, 2026</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="sm">2,048Wh · 2,400W · LiFePO4 · TT-30 RV outlet</text>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Deal information from Dealectric; price and availability not independently verified.</text>
    <text><Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="View deal and purchase"/></text>

The AC200L stands out because it combines a built-in 30-amp-style RV outlet, 2,400W inverter, and up to 1,200W solar input. That makes it practical for RV refrigerators, lights, water pumps, and small kitchen appliances. <Cite ref="turn462053view0"/>

## How it compares

| Model | Listed price | Capacity | AC output | RV suitability |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | $854.05 with code | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Best overall balance |
| Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO | $676 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Best budget value |
| OUPES Mega 2 Pro | $699 | 2,048Wh | 2,500W | Expandable alternative |
| Renogy PowerStation 2000 | $799 | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | Good RV-specific alternative |
| Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 | $899.99 | ~2kWh | — | Lighter at 41.7 lb |

<caption>Prices are from the supplied search results, primarily checked October 30–31, 2026. The Anker's output was not established in those results. <Cite ref="turn462053view0"/></caption>

## Important RV considerations

- **30A outlet doesn't mean 30A output.** The AC200L's 2,400W inverter provides about 20A at 120V, not a full 30A RV hookup.
- **Rooftop air conditioning is a challenge.** A typical RV air conditioner can draw substantial power and may exceed startup or runtime limits.
- **Watch your RV converter.** It can consume power charging the house battery, reducing runtime.
- **Solar matters.** The AC200L supports up to 1,200W solar input, useful for longer off-grid trips.

## Bottom line

I'd choose the **BLUETTI AC200L at $854.05** for its combination of RV connectivity, solar charging, and capacity. However, the **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at about $676** is compelling if minimizing cost is your priority.

One caveat: the AC200L is an older model, reportedly discontinued in Canada, so check US warranty support and final checkout pricing before purchasing.

**One question:** Are you planning to run your RV's rooftop air conditioner, or mainly the fridge, lights, water pump, and electronics? That makes a big difference in which power station I'd recommend.
